claim.pdf_says:
c) If the TEST AFTER phrase is specified, and there is one or more AFTER phrase, the following occurs:
    1. The specified set of statements is executed.
    2. The rightmost condition-2 is then evaluated.
    3. If the rightmost condition-2 is false, ... and execution proceeds with step a.
    4. If the last condition evaluated is true, ...
        NOTE After successful execution of the PERFORM statement, all induction variables contain the values they had at the completion of the last execution of the specified set of statements.
claim.markdown_says:
c) If the TEST AFTER phrase is specified, and there is one or more AFTER phrase, the following occurs:

   1\. The specified set of statements is executed.

   2\. The rightmost condition-2 is then evaluated.

   3\. If the rightmost condition-2 is false, the associated induction variable is incremented by the associated augment value, and execution proceeds with step a.

   4\. If the last condition evaluated is true, ...

   NOTE After successful execution of the PERFORM statement, all induction variables contain the values they had at the completion of the last execution of the specified set of statements.
claim.why_it_matters: The numbered steps 1-4 (and the NOTE under step 4) are printed as sub-items of PERFORM general rule 9 c), indented one level deeper; the transcription places them at the same indentation as items a)-e), so they read as siblings of c) rather than its body, and the trailing NOTE reads as applying to the whole of rule 9.
claim.note: Wording is exact; only the list nesting is lost. The same flattening continues onto page 572 (p572-1).

verdict.reasoning: Rendered page 571 (printed 547) at 300 dpi. The printed page indents steps 1.-4. under c), and the NOTE further under step 4. The markdown has every word of c), 1.-4. and the NOTE, in the same order, verbatim. The only difference is indentation depth. The nesting cannot be misread: the steps use a different numbering style (1., 2., ...) from the lettered items a)-e), they follow c)'s lead-in 'the following occurs:', and d) resumes the lettered sequence right after them. Step 3's 'proceeds with step a' is wording from the standard, not a transcription artifact. Notes are informative, so the NOTE's indentation level has no normative effect, and its text is about the TEST AFTER loop anyway. The claim itself says the wording is exact. This is a formatting and layout difference that does not change the meaning, so it is rejected.
